maps.title: Samogitian borderland
maps.note: The prototype map: the forests and bogs of the Grand Duchy against the river and roads of the Order, a grove in the middle.

maps.title: Grunwald
maps.note: 15 July 1410. Poland and Lithuania crushed the Teutonic Order on open upland among woods, lakes and bogs between Grunwald, Stębark and Łodwigowo; the Grand Master fell.

maps.title: Koronowo
maps.note: 10 October 1410. Three months after Grunwald the Polish army beat the Order's mercenaries at Koronowo in three bouts with a truce between them; their commander was taken.

maps.title: Dąbki
maps.note: 13 September 1431. Peasants of the Krajna and a few knights charged from the edge of the plateau on a Livonian force plundering the Noteć meadows; the Order's horse drowned in the bogs and the Marshal of Livonia was taken.

maps.title: Wiłkomierz
maps.note: 1 September 1435. By lake Žirnajai near Ukmergė Sigismund Kęstutaitis caught Švitrigaila's army and the Livonian knights on the march, cut it in two and routed it; the Livonian Master fell.

maps.title: Chojnice
maps.note: 18 September 1454. The Polish levy of Casimir IV charged across the causeway by the lake at Chojnice; the Order's wagon fort held, a sally from the town struck their rear and they fled into the lake and bogs.

maps.title: Świecino
maps.note: 17 September 1462. Piotr Dunin's small army behind its wagons by a muddy lake in the Kashubian beech woods beat the Order: a feigned retreat drew the knights onto hidden crossbowmen.

maps.title: Vedrosha
maps.note: 14 July 1500. Hetman Ostrogski drove the Muscovite vanguard over the Trosna and crossed by the bridge; an ambush from the wood struck his rear and broke the bridge.

maps.title: Lake Smolino
maps.note: 13 September 1502. Falling back from Pskov, Master Plettenberg gave battle by lake Smolino; his foot with guns and the heavy horse of the Landmarshal held off a far larger Muscovite army.

maps.title: Kletsk
maps.note: 5 August 1506. Michael Glinski's Lithuanian army found the Crimean camp on the boggy Lan near Kletsk, built two crossings under its guns, struck from two sides and freed thousands of captives.

maps.title: Łopuszno
maps.note: 28 April 1512. After a night march the Crown hetman Kamieniecki and Prince Konstanty Ostrogski caught the Crimean horde with its captives in a forest corridor by Łopuszno near Wiśniowiec; the freed captives struck the Tatars from behind.

maps.title: Orsha
maps.note: 8 September 1514. Hetman Ostrogski bridged the Dnieper by Orsha in secret and gave battle on the Krapivna field; a feigned retreat, the fire of his foot and his horse broke the Muscovites, many died in the boggy Krapivna.
